name: Helping Hand for Relief and Development
mission: Helping Hand for Relief and Development is a global humanitarian relief and development organization responding to human sufferings in emergency and disastrous situations anywhere all over the world regardless race, gender, ethnicity, class, location, religion, color, cultural diversity and social background; with special focus on countries where the massive population is living below the poverty line. In addition to our emergency relief efforts in natural or man made disaster areas, we also work on long term relief and development programs like livelihood, economic empowerment, orphan and widows support program and skill development program.
theoryOfChange: HHRD recognizes education as a basic human right and one of the most direct and viable pathways out of poverty. We believe that graduating from a four-year degree program after intermediate is the most effective means for our students to earn higher lifetime incomes, have better health outcomes, and enjoy fulfilling lives.

rich_narrative.summary: Helping Hand for Relief and Development (HHRD) is a global humanitarian organization that provides emergency relief and long-term social services to vulnerable populations [4]. The organization maintains a <cite id="1">perfect 100/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a high standard of accountability and financial health. In FY2023, HHRD reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $94,048,415</cite>, though the most recent filing shows a <cite id="3">revenue decline to $89,337,007 in FY2024</cite>. Despite this slight contraction, the charity remains highly efficient, directing a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 91.2%</cite> toward its core missions. This efficiency is further evidenced by its <cite id="1">fundraising efficiency of $0.06 per $1 raised</cite>, which significantly outperforms the 75% industry benchmark. HHRD is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite> and serves several asnaf categories, including the poor and needy [2]. Its programs span <cite id="4">orphan support, healthcare, and education</cite> across regions like Pakistan, Jordan, and Palestine [4][5]. While the <cite id="1">cost per beneficiary is high at $1,996.07</cite>, this reflects a model of direct service delivery and intensive support rather than light-touch aid.
